question.text: Advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma in Thai women: should we continue to offer second-look laparotomy?
question.context: To determine survival among patients with epithelial ovarian carcinoma (EOC) who underwent a second-look laparotomy (SLL) and those refusing the procedure. Also to analyze factor(s) influencing the survival of the patients. Medical records were reviewed of patients with advanced EOC who were clinically free of disease after primary surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy between January 1, 1992, and December 31, 1998. All of them were offered SLL. Measurement outcomes include patient survival and disease-free survival. There were 50 patients with clinically complete remission after chemotherapy. Sixteen patients underwent SLL, and thirty-four patients refused the procedure (NSLL). Seven patients (43.8%) were reported to have positive SLL. After the median follow-up time of 35 months, 12 patients had died, and 5 patients were lost to follow-up. The median survival time for patients with SLL was about 60 months. Five-year survival rates of patients in the SLL, and NSLL groups were 37 per cent (95%CI = 7%-69%), and 88 per cent (95%CI = 65%-96%) respectively (P<0.001). The median time to relapse was about 25 months for patients with negative SLL. Five-year disease-free survival rates of patients in the negative SLL, and NSLL groups were 28 per cent (95%CI = 4%-59%), and 54 per cent (95%CI = 34%-70%) respectively (P=0.251). By Cox regression analysis, tumor grade was the only significant prognostic factor influencing patients' survival (HR = 6, 95%CI of HR = 1.2-34.2).

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates a significantly lower five-year survival rate (37%) in patients who underwent second-look laparotomy (SLL) compared to those who refused the procedure (88%). This suggests that SLL may not be beneficial and could potentially be harmful. The only significant prognostic factor identified was tumor grade, indicating that SLL does not improve survival in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The five-year survival rates of patients with SLL (37%) are significantly lower than those without SLL (88%) (P<0.001).
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While other factors might influence survival, the study's Cox regression analysis highlights tumor grade as the only significant prognostic factor. This suggests that SLL is not a reliable method for identifying patients who would benefit from further treatment, and the procedure itself may not improve outcomes.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study shows that patients who refused second-look laparotomy (NSLL) had significantly better 5-year survival (88% vs 37%) and disease-free survival (54% vs 28%) compared to those who underwent SLL. The data indicates that SLL is associated with poorer outcomes, suggesting it may not be beneficial for advanced epithelial ovarian carcinoma patients.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The 5-year survival rate was significantly lower (37% vs 88%) and disease-free survival was also lower (28% vs 54%) in the SLL group compared to the NSLL group (P<0.001 for survival, P=0.251 for disease-free survival).
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: No other treatment options were presented in the case, but the data clearly shows that refusing SLL is associated with better outcomes, suggesting SLL may not be the optimal treatment for this patient population.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study shows significantly worse survival in patients who underwent second-look laparotomy (SLL) compared to those who refused it (37% vs 88% 5-year survival, P<0.001). This suggests SLL may not be beneficial and could even be harmful, given the high rate of positive findings (43.8%) and poor outcomes. The only significant prognostic factor was tumor grade, not SLL.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Five-year survival rates were 37% for SLL group vs 88% for NSLL group (P<0.001), indicating worse survival with SLL.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Considered whether SLL might identify occult disease for early treatment, but the data show it correlates with worse survival, suggesting it may be misleading or harmful; thus, it is not recommended.

olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Other surgical procedures (e.g., cytoreductive surgery) might have been performed in both groups, but the absence of survival benefit from SLL specifically in this cohort, and the clear inferior outcome for SLL recipients, makes the case against continuing to offer SLL routinely.
